scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original ten-question A1 draft for Mia's short reading story; teacher content approval pending.

tabs.title: Understanding the Story
tabs.description: Understand the main ideas and the people.

tabs.title: Using What You Read
tabs.description: Use the ideas in simple situations.

questions.q: Why is Mia worried at the start?
choices: Her friend is not at school.
She cannot find her book.
She finds some words difficult.
Her teacher gives her no time.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph describes Mia's difficulty with new words and the start of the reading task.

questions.q: What does Mia do when she cannot understand a sentence?
choices: She closes the book.
She makes a small mark next to it.
She goes home.
She asks for a new story.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph describes Mia's difficulty with new words and the start of the reading task.

questions.q: What does Leo want Mia to do first?
choices: Forget the story.
Ask for a different book.
Read only the last page.
Try reading the story again.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph shows how Mia and Leo use rereading, a picture and a notebook.

questions.q: Why does Leo show Mia a picture?
choices: It can help her understand a word.
It is a picture of her family.
He wants her to draw it.
He cannot read the story.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph shows how Mia and Leo use rereading, a picture and a notebook.

questions.q: What does Mia do with two new words?
choices: She sends them to her brother.
She leaves them out of the story.
She writes them in her notebook.
She writes them on her hand.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph shows how Mia and Leo use rereading, a picture and a notebook.

questions.q: How does Mia feel about her reading on Friday?
choices: She is happy because she understands more.
She is angry with Leo.
She thinks every story is now easy.
She wants to stop reading.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph shows progress through practice and Mia reading to her brother.

questions.q: Why is Mia's second story important?
choices: It shows that Mia knows every word.
It shows that practising can help.
It teaches Leo a new word.
It is a story about trains.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph shows progress through practice and Mia reading to her brother.

questions.q: You see a new word next to a picture. What can you do?
choices: Stop reading the whole story.
Write down a different word.
Close the notebook.
Look at the picture to help with the word.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph shows how Mia and Leo use rereading, a picture and a notebook.

questions.q: Your little brother asks you to read again. What did Mia do in this situation?
choices: She put the story away.
She read the lines again.
She asked Leo to come home.
She gave him a new book.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph shows progress through practice and Mia reading to her brother.

questions.q: A story is difficult today. Which plan is closest to Mia's idea?
choices: Wait until every word is easy.
Try only a new subject.
Never write down words.
Read again and ask for help with hard words.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph describes Mia's difficulty with new words and the start of the reading task.
